title: The source local ring is made of polynomial fractions in normalized section coefficients
statement: Let k be a field, X a k-scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], U₀ an open of X, L an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module], r a natural number, and s_j for j in Fin r global sections of L. Assume the tensor pullbacks of the s_j generate L on U₀ [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections; def-pc-module-pullback], and the resulting morphism U₀ → P(Fin r;k) [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] is an immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let x ∈ U₀, let U be any open containing x, and let e be a free generator of L on U [def-sc-local-free-generator]. Write R = O_(X,x), ρ:k → R for the structure map, and c_j ∈ R for the germ of the coefficient of s_j|_U in e. There are i ∈ Fin r and u ∈ Rˣ with u = c_i such that every a ∈ R has a polynomial-fraction presentation: there exist p,q ∈ k[Z_j | j ∈ Fin r] such that q(u⁻¹c_j) is a unit and a q(u⁻¹c_j) = p(u⁻¹c_j), with coefficients evaluated by ρ. There is no closed-point, finite-type, algebraic-closure, or first-order-quotient assumption or conclusion.

proof.text: Work first on an arbitrary source scheme Y over Spec k with its generating family and local frame. The proved generatingSections_pair supplies the section-preserving pullback isomorphism. Choose a standard chart containing the image point using iSup_standardOpen; this also excludes an empty coordinate set without a separate cardinality argument. On the intersection with the frame open, the denominator section and the frame are both free generators, so they differ by a unit. Apply the frame coefficient map and the germ map to map_eq_coordRatio_smul_of_twistRestrict_iso. This identifies every pulled-back coordinate ratio with the inverse of that unit times the corresponding coefficient germ.

The adopted source theorem closure_range_appLE_union_range_coordRatio shows that chart sections are generated by base functions and the coordinate ratios. Since the base is Spec k, GammaSpecIso identifies its global sections with k. Show that both generating sets lie in the range of polynomial evaluation (constants and variables), proving that evaluation onto the chart ring is surjective. The chart is affine. Lift a source-stalk element through the surjective stalk map of the immersion and use IsLocalization.surj for the affine-open stalk localization. Lift its numerator and denominator to polynomials; the denominator maps to a unit. The over-Spec-k identity identifies evaluation on constants with the source structure map, and the ratio identity from the first step identifies evaluation on variables. This proves the local fraction formula on Y.

Apply that result to Y=U0 and the given tensor-pulled-back module. Uniqueness of left adjoints compares tensor pullback with Mathlib pullback, preserving the units. The pulled-back local frame is free, and semilinearity and naturality of the unit show that its coefficients are the pullbacks of the original coefficients. The open inclusion induces a stalk ring isomorphism; transport the unit and fraction equations through its inverse. Finally rename the ULift-indexed polynomial variables along ULift.down. Evaluation commutes with both this renaming and the stalk ring isomorphism, giving exactly the prescribed Fin r formula.

IsLocalization.surj expresses elements of an already specified localization as a numerator divided by a denominator from the inverted submonoid. It supplies the final step after the projective chart and coefficient identifications, not those identifications.

Mathlib localization fraction results and applications. Direct project search also read the proved ProjectiveMorphismChartPreimage and ProjectiveSpace.ChartSections interfaces; no existing theorem gives the stated local-fraction presentation in the prescribed frame.

theorem immersiveSystem_source_local_fractions
    (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    (U₀ : X.Opens) (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible]
    (r : ℕ) (s : Fin r → Γ(L, ⊤))
    (hgen : Epi (((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback U₀.ι).obj L).freeHomEquiv.symm
      (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin r) ↦ SheafOfModules.unitHomEquiv _
        (Scheme.Modules.homOfGlobalSection _
          (Scheme.Modules.tensorSectionsUnit U₀.ι L (s i.down))))))
    [IsImmersion (@ProjectiveSpace.homOfGeneratingSections
      (ULift.{u} (Fin r)) inferInstance U₀.toScheme (Spec (.of k))
      (U₀.ι ≫ (X ↘ Spec (.of k))) ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback U₀.ι).obj L)
      (Scheme.Modules.IsInvertible.of_iso
        (((Classical.choose (Scheme.Modules.exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction U₀.ι)).leftAdjointUniq
          (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction U₀.ι)).app L).symm)
      (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin r) ↦ SheafOfModules.unitHomEquiv _
        (Scheme.Modules.homOfGlobalSection _
          (Scheme.Modules.tensorSectionsUnit U₀.ι L (s i.down)))) hgen)]
    (x : X) (hxU₀ : x ∈ U₀)
    (U : X.Opens) (hxU : x ∈ U) (e : Γ(L, U))
    (he : Scheme.Modules.IsFreeGenerator e) :
    let ρ : k →+* X.presheaf.stalk x :=
      ((X.presheaf.germ ⊤ x trivial).hom.comp (X ↘ Spec (.of k)).appTop.hom).comp
        (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv.hom
    let c : Fin r → X.presheaf.stalk x := fun j ↦
      X.presheaf.germ U x hxU
        (he.coeff (L.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : U ≤ ⊤)).op (s j)))
    ∃ (i : Fin r) (u : (X.presheaf.stalk x)ˣ), (u : X.presheaf.stalk x) = c i ∧
      ∀ a : X.presheaf.stalk x, ∃ p q : MvPolynomial (Fin r) k,
        IsUnit (MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom ρ (fun j ↦ (↑u⁻¹ : X.presheaf.stalk x) * c j) q) ∧
        a * MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom ρ (fun j ↦ (↑u⁻¹ : X.presheaf.stalk x) * c j) q =
          MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom ρ (fun j ↦ (↑u⁻¹ : X.presheaf.stalk x) * c j) p
